36787376.model_family: deep learning models (convolutional neural network on pressure-volume tracings; imaging model on fluoroscopic images; ensemble)
36787376.clinical_problem: classifying severity of neurogenic bladder dysfunction from videourodynamics in children with spina bifida
36787376.patient_population: patients aged 2 months to 28 years with spina bifida undergoing videourodynamics at a single institution (306 studies)
36787376.model_description: Inputs are videourodynamics pressure-volume tracings and fluoroscopic bladder images; four models (a random forest clinical model, a CNN on the pressure-volume signal, a CNN on fluoroscopic images, and an ensemble of the two CNNs) classify bladder dysfunction severity as none/mild, moderate, or severe.
36787376.headline_result: ensemble model accuracy 70% (95% CI 66-76%), weighted kappa 0.54, outperforming a clinical-data-only model (accuracy 61%, kappa 0.37)
36787376.study_design: retrospective single-center cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study

35135639.clinical_problem: identifying children at risk of suicidal thoughts or behaviors using clinical, cognitive, neuroimaging and genetic risk factors
35135639.patient_population: 5,885 children ages 9-11 from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study, validated in 1,712 children from seven independent sites
35135639.model_description: Inputs are sociodemographic, clinical-psychiatric, cognitive, neuroimaging and genetic characteristics; a penalized logistic regression model classifies children with current or past suicidal thoughts/behaviors versus clinical and healthy controls.
35135639.dataset_size: 5,885 children (ABCD study); validation n=1,712 from 7 independent sites
35135639.headline_result: AUROC 0.80-0.81 distinguishing suicidal-thoughts/behaviors group from healthy controls; 0.71-0.77 versus clinical controls; could not distinguish ideation from attempt (AUROC 0.49-0.58)
35135639.study_design: cross-sectional multi-site cohort study (ABCD) with machine learning classification and external validation

32833630.model_family: self-supervised generative adversarial network with cross-modal attention
32833630.clinical_problem: synthesizing MRI-like images from prenatal ultrasound to aid non-expert interpretation of fetal brain anatomy and support US-MRI registration/fusion
32833630.patient_population: fetal brain ultrasound and MRI imaging (unpaired datasets)
32833630.model_description: Input is a clinical fetal brain ultrasound image; output is a synthesized MRI-like image, produced end-to-end and self-supervised (no paired ground-truth data) using adversarial learning in image and feature space plus an adversarial structural constraint and cross-modal attention.
32833630.study_design: retrospective technical development study (self-supervised image synthesis)

29709627.model_family: multi-task machine learning framework with feature selection on neuroimaging measurements
29709627.clinical_problem: predicting future cognitive developmental scores in infants from earlier structural brain MRI, with incomplete longitudinal data
29709627.patient_population: in-house longitudinal infant cohort with neuroimaging from as early as 24 months, cognitive scores measured at age 4
29709627.model_description: Input is longitudinal structural MRI morphometric measurements from infancy (with missing time points handled by the framework); output is a multi-task machine learning prediction of multiple future cognitive scores at age 4.
29709627.headline_result: root mean square error 0.18 for predicting cognitive scores at age 4 using imaging data from as early as 24 months
29709627.study_design: prospective longitudinal cohort study with multi-task machine learning

35751051.model_family: deep convolutional neural network with transfer learning
35751051.clinical_problem: predicting the risk of curve progression in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis from spine radiographs
35751051.patient_population: 58 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (mean age 12.5 years), Cobb angle 10-25 degrees
35751051.model_description: Input is spine radiographs from three regions of interest (lung, abdomen, total spine); output is a predicted probability of scoliosis curve progression (Cobb angle increase >10 degrees within two years), produced by a deep CNN with transfer learning and compared against five spine surgeons.
35751051.headline_result: DCNN accuracy 69%, AUC 0.70, versus spine surgeons' accuracy of 47%

36049595.model_family: convolutional neural network for view classification
36049595.clinical_problem: automated view classification of pediatric echocardiograms as a step toward fully automated echocardiogram interpretation
36049595.patient_population: patients aged 0-19 years undergoing echocardiography, plus a separate cohort of children with leukemia undergoing cardiac surveillance
36049595.model_description: Input is a pediatric echocardiographic image; output is a classification into one of 27 preselected standard pediatric echocardiographic views (anatomic sweeps, color Doppler, Doppler tracings), trained and tested across the pediatric age spectrum and in a leukemia surveillance cohort.
36049595.dataset_size: 12,067 training images; 6,197 validation images; 9,684 test images from 100 patients; a second test set of 524 echocardiograms from children with leukemia
36049595.headline_result: 27-view classification accuracy 90.3% overall; in the leukemia cohort, per-study positive predictive value 98.7-99.2% and sensitivity 76.9-94.8%
36049595.study_design: retrospective single-center technical development and validation study

34044207.model_family: machine learning classification comparing behavioral, cognitive and neuroimaging predictors
34044207.clinical_problem: evaluating whether adding neuroimaging and neurocognitive assessments improves machine-learning-based ADHD diagnosis in young children beyond behavior ratings
34044207.model_description: Inputs are parent/teacher behavior ratings, behavioral executive-function measures, and neuroimaging (cortical anatomy) measures; machine learning models compare the predictive value of each input type for classifying ADHD versus typically developing children.
34044207.headline_result: teacher ratings of executive function were the most predictive of ADHD; neuroimaging measures of cortical anatomy added little incremental predictive value
34044207.study_design: cross-sectional single-center machine learning classification study

34789725.clinical_problem: identifying sensitive periods and types of childhood maltreatment associated with oxytocin-gene methylation and its effects on brain structure/function
34789725.model_description: Input is multi-modal brain MRI (voxel-based morphometry, diffusion tensor imaging, task and resting-state fMRI) and salivary DNA methylation data; a random forest regression model identifies which maltreatment age and type most contribute to an oxytocin methylation index, which is then related to brain structure and function.
34789725.headline_result: sensitive period ages 5-8 and physical abuse contributed most to the oxytocin methylation index; index was negatively correlated with left superior parietal lobule gray matter volume
34789725.study_design: case-control multi-modal MRI study with random forest analysis

34957233.clinical_problem: segmenting the tricuspid valve from 3D echocardiography in children with hypoplastic left heart syndrome to support surgical planning
34957233.patient_population: children with hypoplastic left heart syndrome undergoing transthoracic 3D echocardiography (133 training, 28 validation image-segmentation pairs)
34957233.model_description: Input is a transthoracic 3D echocardiogram of the tricuspid valve, with an optional annular curve and commissural landmarks; output is a fully convolutional network segmentation of the tricuspid valve leaflets, to enable rapid modeling and quantification for surgical planning.
34957233.release_evidence: "We are now working to deploy this network for public use" (not yet released at time of publication)
34957233.dataset_size: 133 training and 28 validation 3D echocardiogram image-segmentation pairs
34957233.headline_result: median Dice similarity coefficient 0.86 for merged tricuspid valve segmentation, mean boundary distance 0.35 mm

31022245.clinical_problem: developing an interpretable machine learning model to aid ADHD diagnosis using neuroimaging and phenotypic data
31022245.patient_population: sample from the public ADHD-200 dataset (children and adolescents)
31022245.model_description: Input is neuroimaging and phenotypic data from the ADHD-200 collection; output is an ADHD-versus-typically-developing classification produced by a decision tree chosen for its readability, highlighting the limbic system as a relevant predictor.
31022245.study_design: retrospective public-dataset (ADHD-200) machine learning study emphasizing interpretability

25933215.model_family: Fisher vector encoding of RootSIFT features with a support vector machine classifier
25933215.clinical_problem: automated recognition of fetal facial standard planes during ultrasound examination for biometric measurement and diagnosis
25933215.patient_population: fetal ultrasound images used for standard-plane classification
25933215.model_description: Input is a 2D fetal ultrasound image; output is classification of the image as an axial, coronal, or sagittal fetal facial standard plane, using densely sampled RootSIFT features encoded with a Fisher vector and classified by an SVM.
25933215.headline_result: accuracy 93.27% and mean average precision 99.19% recognizing fetal facial standard planes

24917530.clinical_problem: differentiating children/adolescents with bipolar disorder from healthy controls using amygdala structural MRI features
24917530.patient_population: 16 children/adolescents with unmedicated DSM-IV bipolar disorder and 16 matched healthy controls
24917530.model_description: Input is voxel-based gray matter morphometric features from a bilateral amygdala region of interest on structural T1 MRI; output is a multivariate pattern analysis classification of bipolar disorder versus healthy control status for individual, previously unseen subjects.
24917530.dataset_size: 16 children/adolescents with bipolar disorder, 16 healthy controls
24917530.study_design: retrospective case-control MRI machine learning study

24108712.model_family: Random Forest with feature selection and weighted voting (novel method)
24108712.clinical_problem: improving 3-D random-forest-based image segmentation accuracy, demonstrated on fetal femur ultrasound bone-length measurement and adult brain MRI segmentation
24108712.patient_population: adult brain MRI dataset and 3-D fetal femoral ultrasound dataset
24108712.model_description: Input is a 3D medical image (adult brain MRI or fetal femur ultrasound); output is a voxel classification/segmentation produced by an enhanced Random Forest framework that selects strong features and weights each decision tree, compared against a traditional Random Forest.
24108712.headline_result: notable improvement in segmentation accuracy over traditional Random Forest, on both adult brain MRI and 3D fetal femoral ultrasound datasets
24108712.study_design: retrospective technical method-development study evaluated on multiple datasets

39449887.exclusion_reason: review of digital dementia/screen time, non-imaging

37992593.model_family: Gaussian Mixture Model subtyping; amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF) analysis
37992593.clinical_problem: subtyping depression to guide targeted repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS)
37992593.patient_population: 238 major depressive disorder patients and 66 healthy controls at Center 1 (subtyping); 72 hospitalized depressed youths at Center 2 (treatment application)
37992593.model_description: Resting-state fMRI amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF) maps are input to a Gaussian Mixture Model that clusters depressed patients into two neuroimaging subtypes (archetypal and atypical); subtype membership then selects an rTMS target region (dorsomedial prefrontal cortex or occipital cortex) applied to hospitalized depressed youths.
37992593.dataset_size: 238 MDD patients and 66 healthy controls (Center 1); 72 hospitalized depressed youths (Center 2)
37992593.headline_result: symptom response 90.00% in archetypal depression and 70.73% in atypical depression after subtype-targeted rTMS
37992593.study_design: two-stage multicenter development and clinical application study

38666133.model_family: support vector machine on graph-based morphological network features
38666133.clinical_problem: distinguishing adolescents with major depressive disorder from healthy controls using structural brain network topology
38666133.patient_population: 25 first-episode, treatment-naive adolescents with MDD and 19 healthy controls
38666133.model_description: T1-weighted MRI is used to build single-subject morphological brain networks (based on cortical thickness, fractal dimension, gyrification index, sulcus depth); graph-based topological features from the cortical-thickness network are fed into a support vector machine that outputs a binary MDD-vs-healthy-control classification.
38666133.headline_result: 87.6% accuracy distinguishing adolescent MDD from healthy controls using cortical-thickness network topology
38666133.study_design: retrospective single-center case-control diagnostic accuracy study

35964072.model_family: deep transfer learning (13 CNN architectures, best DarkNet53)
35964072.clinical_problem: detecting developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) on pelvic X-ray
35964072.patient_population: 354 subjects (120 DDH, 234 normal) from two hospitals in northern Jordan
35964072.model_description: Pelvic anteroposterior X-ray images are classified as DDH or normal by thirteen deep transfer-learning CNN models, without requiring explicit angle measurements; the best-performing model (DarkNet53) is reported.
35964072.headline_result: DarkNet53: 96.3% accuracy, F1 95%, precision 90.6%, recall 100%, specificity 94.3%

33041749.clinical_problem: early prediction of cognitive deficit at 2 years of age in very preterm infants
33041749.patient_population: 110 very preterm infants (≤32 weeks gestational age)
33041749.model_description: Brain structural connectome, derived from diffusion tensor imaging at term-equivalent age and represented as a 2D image, is input to a transfer-learning-enhanced CNN that outputs a cognitive-deficit classification and a continuous cognitive score, predicting Bayley-III cognitive assessment at 2 years of corrected age.

25687738.clinical_problem: distinguishing pediatric unipolar depression from healthy controls using brain structure
25687738.patient_population: 25 pediatric unipolar depression patients and 26 demographically matched healthy controls
25687738.model_description: T1-weighted structural MRI is used to derive multiple neuromorphometric indices (cortical thickness, volume, cortical folding); a support vector machine trained on these indices classifies individual subjects as having pediatric unipolar depression or being a healthy control.
25687738.dataset_size: 25 pediatric unipolar depression patients, 26 healthy controls
25687738.study_design: retrospective single-center case-control diagnostic accuracy study

25485393.model_family: stacked auto-encoder (deep learning) with sparse patch matching
25485393.clinical_problem: segmenting the hippocampus on infant brain MRI to study early brain development
25485393.model_description: T1- and T2-weighted infant brain MRI are input to a Stacked Auto Encoder that learns deep feature representations combining both contrasts; these learned features drive a sparse patch-matching method that transfers hippocampus labels from multiple atlases onto a new infant image, producing a hippocampus segmentation.

20681014.exclusion_reason: adult word-learning fMRI study, no pediatric population

19342936.exclusion_reason: computer algorithm/statistical clustering, no AI/ML model

35396036.clinical_problem: prenatal detection and diagnosis of congenital heart disease on fetal echocardiography
35396036.patient_population: fetuses undergoing fetal echocardiography for suspected congenital heart disease
35396036.model_description: Narrative review describing how AI algorithms applied to fetal echocardiography could improve image acquisition, image optimization, automated measurements, outlier identification, diagnostic classification, and outcome prediction for congenital heart disease; no single model is developed.

32714147.exclusion_reason: animal (mouse) model study, not human imaging

31521335.exclusion_reason: adult/young-adult alcohol relapse fMRI study, not pediatric

23922750.body_region: fetal brain (frontal lobe, basal ganglia, mesencephalon, cerebellum)
23922750.clinical_problem: predicting abnormal neonatal neurobehavior in small-for-gestational-age fetuses from fetal brain MRI texture
23922750.patient_population: 91 small-for-gestational-age fetuses at 37 weeks gestational age
23922750.model_description: Quantitative texture features are extracted from fetal MRI of the frontal lobe, basal ganglia, mesencephalon and cerebellum; machine learning models these textural features to predict abnormal neonatal neurobehavior (NBAS test) after birth.
23922750.headline_result: prediction accuracy 95.12% frontal lobe, 95.56% basal ganglia, 93.18% mesencephalon, 83.33% cerebellum

24095098.clinical_problem: classifying adolescent idiopathic scoliosis curve types and predicting surgical fusion levels
24095098.patient_population: 1,776 patients surgically treated for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
24095098.model_description: Cobb angles and curve geometry measured on spine radiographs are input to a Kohonen self-organizing map (a type of artificial neural network) that clusters patients into curve-type nodes; the map's clustering is compared with the Lenke classification and surgeons' actual fusion-level choices.
24095098.headline_result: topographic error 0.02; Lenke classification predicted fused regions in 46% of individual cases vs. 82% of SOM nodes
24095098.study_design: retrospective multicenter analysis with technical concept development

22307098.exclusion_reason: computerized lung sound (auscultation) analysis, non-radiologic imaging

22959658.model_family: machine learning-based automatic segmentation and classification
22959658.clinical_problem: assisting ADHD diagnosis via caudate nucleus volumetric abnormalities
22959658.patient_population: pediatric population with and without ADHD
22959658.model_description: Brain MRI is segmented into internal and external caudate nucleus structures using a machine-learning-based automatic segmentation method; new volume-relation features (3D Dissociated Dipoles) are then used to classify subjects for ADHD diagnostic assistance.
22959658.study_design: retrospective single-center method development and evaluation

37163546.model_family: support vector machine on structural and functional MRI features
37163546.clinical_problem: identifying brain structural and functional abnormalities to distinguish young children with autism spectrum disorder from typically developing children
37163546.patient_population: 67 children with ASD (aged 2-7 years) and 39 age-matched typically developing controls
37163546.model_description: Structural (voxel-based morphometry) and resting-state functional MRI features are combined and input to a support vector machine that classifies children as having autism spectrum disorder or being typically developing.
37163546.dataset_size: 67 children with ASD, 39 typically developing controls
37163546.headline_result: 86.2% accuracy discriminating ASD from typically developing children using combined structural and functional features
37163546.study_design: retrospective single-center case-control diagnostic accuracy study

37666981.clinical_problem: automatic measurement of the Cobb angle for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
37666981.patient_population: patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis undergoing full-spine standing X-ray
37666981.model_description: A convolutional neural network automatically detects vertebrae on full-length spine X-rays and measures the Cobb angle; its output is compared with manual measurements from six physicians.
37666981.headline_result: ICC 0.973 for major curve vs. six physicians; AI measured 1.7-2.2° smaller than physicians

34346086.model_family: resting-state dynamic causal modeling-based support vector machine (rs-DCM-SVM)
34346086.clinical_problem: diagnosing drug-naive Rolandic epilepsy from resting-state brain network imbalance
34346086.patient_population: discovery cohort: 76 children with Rolandic epilepsy and 76 normal controls; replication cohort: 59 children with Rolandic epilepsy and 60 normal controls
34346086.model_description: Resting-state fMRI functional connectivity across seven canonical neural networks is analyzed with dynamic causal modeling, and an SVM classifier trained on these excitatory/inhibitory-imbalance features distinguishes children with Rolandic epilepsy from normal controls.
34346086.study_design: multicenter case-control diagnostic accuracy study with discovery and replication cohorts

32607611.model_family: principal component analysis + support vector machine
32607611.clinical_problem: distinguishing pediatric mild traumatic brain injury from typically developing controls when conventional imaging is normal
32607611.patient_population: 24 adolescents (14 with mild TBI, 10 typically developing controls), aged 10-16 years
32607611.model_description: Diffusion MRI fiber tractography is used to compute edge density imaging maps of brain connectivity; PCA and an SVM classifier applied to these maps distinguish mild TBI from typically developing controls, compared against neurocognitive tests and conventional fractional anisotropy.
32607611.headline_result: sensitivity 79%, specificity 100%, AUC 94% for edge density imaging + SVM-PCA
32607611.study_design: prospective single-center proof-of-concept diagnostic accuracy study

23299250.exclusion_reason: computational cognitive model of category learning, not applied to radiologic images

21347746.clinical_problem: bone age assessment in young children
21347746.patient_population: children aged 0 to 6 years from a digital hand atlas
21347746.model_description: An automated edge-following technique extracts carpal bone boundaries from hand X-rays; five features derived from these boundaries are input to a support vector regression model that outputs an estimated bone age, compared against radiologist ground truth.
21347746.dataset_size: 180 carpal bone images from a digital hand atlas
21347746.headline_result: SVR results very close to skilled radiologists' bone age assessments (leave-one-out cross-validation), outperforming neural-network regression

23976891.exclusion_reason: statistical regression of cerebral blood flow and IQ, no AI/ML

20614370.exclusion_reason: fMRI activation study of relational aggression, no AI/ML

19418048.clinical_problem: detecting pulmonary nodules in pediatric oncology patients
19418048.patient_population: 24 children (age 3-18 years) with known primary tumors and lung nodules
19418048.model_description: Chest CT scans are analyzed by a commercially available computer-aided detection system that flags candidate pulmonary nodules; CAD sensitivity is compared against four radiologists, stratified by nodule size and location.
19418048.headline_result: CAD sensitivity 34% overall (80% for nodules ≥4mm) vs. radiologist sensitivity 68-79%; 0.9 CAD false positives per study
19418048.study_design: retrospective single-center diagnostic accuracy / reader-comparison study

17653705.exclusion_reason: review of quantitative MRI methods, no specific AI/ML model described

38165551.model_family: 3D residual neural network (multimodal, fusing low-dose CT)
38165551.clinical_problem: reducing pediatric total-body PET/CT scan time (and sedation need) while preserving image quality
38165551.patient_population: 270 pediatric patients undergoing total-body 18F-FDG PET/CT (uEXPLORER scanner)
38165551.model_description: Short-duration PET list-mode data (6-150 s) and low-dose CT images are fused as input to a 3D residual convolutional neural network that outputs a full-length, high-dose-quality PET image, aiming to shorten scan time without sedation-related motion artifacts.
38165551.headline_result: 60-second multimodal AI reconstruction produced PET image quality comparable to the full 600-second acquisition
38165551.study_design: retrospective single-center technical development and evaluation

38319162.clinical_problem: reducing gadolinium-based contrast agent use in brain tumor MRI, including in children
38319162.patient_population: pediatric and adult patients with primary brain tumors (gliomas, meningiomas) undergoing MRI
38319162.model_description: Narrative review of strategies to reduce gadolinium-based contrast agent exposure in glioma and meningioma MRI, including reduced/omitted contrast protocols and artificial-intelligence methods that generate synthetic postcontrast images from non-contrast or low-dose scans; no single model is developed.

38355987.exclusion_reason: adult total-body PET/CT study, pediatric only mentioned as future application

38585353.clinical_problem: improving correspondence between low-field and high-field brain MRI in young people
38585353.model_description: T1- and T2-weighted images from a 64mT low-field portable MRI system are processed by SynthSR, a convolutional-neural-network super-resolution method, to produce images with improved correspondence to matched 3T high-field images; performance is compared against a multi-orientation averaging alternative.
38585353.headline_result: SynthSR improved correspondence to high-field images to r=0.85-0.97 for most brain volume measures (vs. r=0.60-0.88 uncorrected); cortical thickness correspondence remained poor (r=0.14)

38809123.clinical_problem: applying AI to pediatric cancer imaging acquisition, processing, diagnosis, staging and treatment-response monitoring
38809123.patient_population: children with cancer undergoing diagnostic imaging
38809123.model_description: Narrative review of current AI applications in pediatric cancer imaging, covering image acquisition, processing, reconstruction, segmentation, diagnosis, staging, and treatment-response monitoring, and the challenges (data scarcity, anatomic diversity, nonstandardized protocols) limiting clinical translation; no single model is developed.

37241224.exclusion_reason: systematic review explicitly excludes pediatric studies

37324652.clinical_problem: using machine learning to assess fetal well-being and predict/diagnose obstetric disease (gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia, preterm birth, fetal growth restriction, fetal anomalies)
37324652.model_description: Narrative review of machine-learning tools for obstetric disease prediction and diagnosis, including automated diagnostic imaging of fetal anomalies and assessment of fetoplacental and cervix function using ultrasound and MRI; no single model is developed.

37467869.model_family: adult-trained deep learning algorithm applied to pediatric images
37467869.clinical_problem: detecting pneumonia on pediatric chest radiographs using an adult-trained AI algorithm
37467869.patient_population: pediatric patients aged 1 to 5 years (publicly available pediatric chest X-ray dataset)
37467869.model_description: A publicly available pediatric chest X-ray dataset is analyzed using an AI pneumonia-detection algorithm from TorchXRayVision that was trained on adult images; a 60% threshold produces a binary pneumonia prediction, compared against dataset labels, to test whether adult-trained algorithms generalize to pediatric patients.
37467869.headline_result: sensitivity 79.83%, specificity 67.66%, accuracy 76.54%, F1 0.83 overall; PPV fell to 69.9% and F1 to 0.74 for viral pneumonia
37467869.study_design: retrospective external validation of an adult-trained algorithm on a pediatric dataset

37536046.model_family: machine learning framework (KNN, logistic regression, linear SVM, RBF-SVM, random forest)
37536046.clinical_problem: diagnosing ADHD using structural brain MRI and personal characteristics
37536046.patient_population: 316 children with ADHD and 316 typically developing children (age-balanced public dataset)
37536046.model_description: Gray-matter volumes (AAL3 atlas) and cortical-thickness features (Destrieux atlas), combined with personal characteristic data, are input to several classifiers (KNN, logistic regression, linear and RBF SVM, random forest) that output an ADHD-vs-typically-developing classification.
37536046.headline_result: maximum classification accuracy 75% (cortical thickness + personal characteristics, RBF-SVM/SVM with ensemble feature selection)
37536046.study_design: retrospective case-control diagnostic accuracy study using a public dataset

34980622.exclusion_reason: adult population breast cancer mammography screening study

35125417.clinical_problem: detecting developmental dysplasia of the hip on infant hip ultrasound sweeps
35125417.patient_population: 240 infant hips (120 single 2D images, 120 sweeps) spanning normal to severe dysplasia
35125417.model_description: Infant hip ultrasound sweeps and single 2D images are read by an FDA-cleared commercial AI software package (Medo Hip), which measures the alpha angle and classifies DDH status; its agreement is compared against 12 human readers of varying experience (radiologists, sonographers, clinicians, DDH subspecialists).
35125417.headline_result: alpha-angle ICC=0.87 (sweeps)/0.90 (single images) vs. subspecialists; DDH diagnosis agreement kappa=0.47 (AI) vs. 0.72 (subspecialists) on sweeps

35144197.model_family: spatio-temporal directed acyclic graph deep learning with attention
35144197.clinical_problem: predicting cognition and age from resting-state functional brain network data
35144197.patient_population: Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development cohort (n=7,693, children) and OASIS-3 cohort (n=1,786, older adults)
35144197.model_description: Resting-state fMRI time series and derived functional connectivity are input to a deep-learning framework combining a spatio-temporal graph convolutional network with a functional-connectivity convolutional network and an attention mechanism, which outputs predicted cognition scores or brain age.
35144197.headline_result: outperformed SVR, elastic-net/random-forest, spatio-temporal graph convolution, and BrainNetCNN baselines (no single summary number given); robust across independent ABCD sites
35144197.study_design: retrospective multicenter method development and validation study

35348867.clinical_problem: automatically evaluating and diagnosing adolescent idiopathic scoliosis on full-spine X-ray
35348867.patient_population: patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis undergoing full spinal anteroposterior X-ray
35348867.model_description: Full-spine anteroposterior X-rays are analyzed by a deep learning ensemble network that automatically measures the Cobb angle, apical vertebrae, and upper/lower vertebrae, and assesses anatomical balance parameters, validated against a public dataset and an external hospital.
35348867.dataset_size: 788 training + 185 internal test images; external validation set from a separate hospital; also validated on a public dataset
35348867.headline_result: Cobb angle accuracy/recall 89.36%/97.35%; mean absolute error 1.07° for Cobb angle; measurement 200x faster than radiologists
35348867.study_design: retrospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study with external validation

35667473.clinical_problem: classifying pediatric posterior fossa brain tumor type (medulloblastoma vs. ependymoma vs. astrocytoma)
35667473.patient_population: 99 pediatric patients with posterior fossa tumors (59 medulloblastoma, 13 ependymoma, 27 astrocytoma), histologically confirmed
35667473.model_description: Whole-tumor radiomic features are extracted from manually segmented MRI (including ADC sequence) and the top ten features selected by a forest-based method are input to a random forest classifier that outputs the histologic tumor type.
35667473.headline_result: validation accuracy 0.938; sensitivity 1.000/0.948/0.808 and specificity 0.952/0.926/1.000 for EP/MB/PA respectively

35741233.clinical_problem: automating Graf standard plane detection and angle measurement for infant hip ultrasound (DDH diagnosis)
35741233.patient_population: infants undergoing hip ultrasound for suspected developmental dysplasia of the hip
35741233.model_description: Hip ultrasound images or video are processed by a three-module deep-learning framework (anatomical-structure detection, standard-plane scoring, angle measurement) that automatically identifies the Graf standard plane and measures alpha/beta angles to classify Graf type I/II hips, in both static-image and dynamic-video modes.
35741233.headline_result: static mode: mean absolute error α 1.71°, β 2.40°, classification accuracy 94.71%; dynamic mode: accuracy 89.51% at 31 fps
35741233.study_design: retrospective technical development and evaluation study

35942441.model_family: boundary-aware grid contextual attention convolutional network
35942441.clinical_problem: segmenting osteosarcoma tumor boundaries on MRI
35942441.model_description: Osteosarcoma MRI images are segmented by a novel network (BA-GCA Net) that combines grid contextual attention, a statistical texture learning block, and a spatial transformer block to better capture tumor texture and boundary despite vague or irregular tumor margins.
35942441.dataset_size: over 80,000 MRI images from the Second Xiangya Hospital
35942441.headline_result: higher segmentation accuracy than existing methods (no single summary metric given), with only a slight increase in parameters/computation
35942441.study_design: retrospective single-center technical development study with ablation experiments

36092792.clinical_problem: measuring the angle of progression to assess fetal head descent during labor
36092792.patient_population: pregnant patients undergoing transperineal ultrasound during labor
36092792.model_description: Transperineal ultrasound images are processed by a multitask network with a shared encoder and three task-specific decoders that recognize the standard imaging plane, segment the pubic symphysis and fetal head, and detect pubic-symphysis endpoints, from which the angle of progression is automatically computed.
36092792.headline_result: standard-plane classification accuracy 92.26%; mean AoP error 3.898° (STD 3.192°); Pearson r=0.964 vs. manual measurement
36092792.study_design: retrospective technical development and agreement study

36140628.model_family: ensemble of eight fine-tuned segmentation architectures (UNet, UNet++, Attention UNet, UNet3+, TransUNet, FPN, LinkNet, Deeplabv3) with EfficientNetB0 backbone
36140628.clinical_problem: segmenting the fetal head on ultrasound and estimating gestational age and fetal weight

34648114.model_description: A ResNet-50 deep convolutional neural network trained on chest radiographs from the Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center is tested on an internal holdout set and on an external NIH ChestXray14 dataset to detect pneumonia; class-activation-mapping heatmaps assess whether the model relies on clinically relevant features.

34707474.clinical_problem: predicting fetal brain age from structural MRI to help identify abnormal brain development

34707474.headline_result: mean absolute error 0.125 weeks internally; 0.508 weeks on external validation

32476702.clinical_problem: segmenting the uterine cavity and placenta on fetal MRI to help detect abnormalities affecting maternal and fetal health

33102411.model_description: Cerebral perfusion values from pulsed arterial spin labeling MRI in brain regions with significant group differences are input to a machine learning model that predicts later language and motor neurodevelopmental outcomes in neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.

32677744.exclusion_reason: Adult women's national survey study on mammography utilization factors; not pediatric, not an image-analysis AI model.

32916543.clinical_problem: Automatic recognition of dyslexia in children using brain activation patterns from task-based fMRI during reading tasks.
32916543.model_description: Three parallel 3D convolutional neural networks, each processing brain activation maps from a different reading task, are concatenated to classify children as dyslexic or not.

32916583.exclusion_reason: Systematic review of ADHD/rolandic epilepsy comorbidity and neuroimaging/EEG findings; not focused on AI/machine learning methods.

33103162.clinical_problem: Learning representations from fetal ultrasound video and sonographer narration without manual annotation, to support standard-plane detection.
33103162.patient_population: Multi-modal fetal ultrasound video and speech-audio dataset
33103162.model_description: Uses cross-modal contrastive learning between ultrasound video and sonographer speech audio (self-supervised, no manual labels) to learn representations transferable to fetal standard-plane detection and eye-gaze prediction.

33363064.exclusion_reason: Non-invasive fetal electrocardiography technique for cardiotocography; not a radiologic imaging modality and no AI/ML component described.

34367687.exclusion_reason: Uses histopathology/biopsy images of the small bowel (Celiac Disease), not radiologic imaging.

31112785.clinical_problem: Correcting topological errors (handles/holes) in reconstructed infant cortical surfaces from brain MRI to enable accurate early brain development studies.
31112785.patient_population: Infant brain MRI (human), also validated on macaque infant MRI
31112785.model_description: An anatomically constrained deep learning network iteratively identifies and corrects candidate voxels with topological defects in segmented infant brain MRI to produce topologically accurate cortical surfaces.
31112785.study_design: retrospective methods development study, validated on simulated and real topological errors

31632332.model_family: machine learning (radiomics: decision tree, SVM, others)
31632332.clinical_problem: Distinguishing neonatal acute bilirubin encephalopathy from normal myelination using MRI radiomics features.
31632332.patient_population: 32 neonates with acute bilirubin encephalopathy, 29 age-matched controls
31632332.model_description: Radiomics texture features extracted from T1-weighted MRI regions of interest are fed into multiple machine learning classifiers (decision tree, SVM, etc.) to distinguish ABE from normal myelination.

31755665.clinical_problem: Predicting persistent post-concussion symptom recovery in children using structural and functional brain MRI markers of the default mode network.
31755665.patient_population: 110 children with mixed recovery following mild traumatic brain injury
31755665.model_description: Combines gray matter volume (voxel-based morphometry) and resting-state functional connectivity MRI features using machine learning to predict individual recovery from persistent post-concussion symptoms.
31755665.headline_result: AUC 0.86 predicting clinical outcome at follow-up

31760495.clinical_problem: Predicting optimal versus suboptimal spontaneous lumbar curve correction after selective thoracic fusion in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis using radiographic parameters.
31760495.patient_population: 71 Lenke 1 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients with 2-year follow-up
31760495.model_description: Radiographic spinal parameters (Cobb angles, kyphosis, rotation, translation) are used as input to a decision tree model that predicts optimal versus suboptimal spontaneous lumbar curve correction after surgery.

31993109.clinical_problem: Automatically describing the clinical workflow of full-length routine fetal anomaly ultrasound scans by classifying scan sections.
31993109.patient_population: Full-length fetal anomaly ultrasound scan videos
31993109.model_description: 2D and 2D+t CNN, LSTM, and convolutional LSTM architectures process full-length fetal ultrasound video to automatically partition and label scan sections for workflow analysis.

28439522.clinical_problem: Automated quality assessment and biometric measurement (biparietal diameter, occipital-frontal diameter, head circumference) of the fetal head on 2D obstetric ultrasound.
28439522.model_description: Texton-based segmentation extracts the fetal head region; shape and anatomic features are fed into a random forest classifier to assess image quality and derive fetal head biometry.
28439522.study_design: retrospective methods development and validation study

28656614.clinical_problem: Automated segmentation of renal cortex, medulla, and collecting system on dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI to estimate glomerular filtration rate in children.
28656614.model_description: A modified iterative graph-cut (GrabCut) segmentation combined with a random forest classifier segments the kidney into cortex, medulla and collecting system from dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI, used to estimate GFR.
28656614.headline_result: F1=0.93 whole-kidney, F1=0.86 cortex; GFR estimation error 2.98+/-0.66%

28852853.clinical_problem: Predicting risk of symptomatic cerebral vasospasm after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage in children using an adult-derived neural network model applied to pediatric clinical and radiographic data.
28852853.patient_population: 16 pediatric patients (<21 years) with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage
28852853.model_description: An artificial neural network trained on adult aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage data is applied to pediatric demographic, clinical, and radiographic variables to output a likelihood score for symptomatic cerebral vasospasm.
28852853.headline_result: ANN correctly predicted all 16 outcomes; mean prediction strength -0.86 (no vasospasm) vs 0.93 (vasospasm case)

27445675.clinical_problem: Identifying a common pattern of structural brain alterations distinguishing young children with autism spectrum disorder from controls using structural MRI.
27445675.patient_population: 41 children with ASD (21M/20F), 40 controls (20M/20F), ages 22-72 months
27445675.model_description: Regional structural features from brain MRI are used to train a one-class support vector machine on the ASD group alone, which then classifies new subjects as ASD or outliers (controls).

27648848.exclusion_reason: Conventional fMRI activation and voxel-based morphometry statistical analysis; no AI/ML classifier described.

25379446.clinical_problem: Determining which white matter tracts independently contribute to language impairment in children with epilepsy and cortical malformations, using diffusion tensor imaging.
25379446.patient_population: 33 pediatric patients with malformations of cortical development and epilepsy, ages 3-18
25379446.model_description: Diffusion tensor imaging metrics (mean diffusivity, fractional anisotropy) from six white matter tracts are analyzed using a random forest machine learning algorithm to determine each tract's independent contribution to language impairment.

25467807.clinical_problem: Automated detection of endotracheal tube presence and tip location on pediatric chest radiographs to identify malposition.
25467807.model_description: Line-tracing features from the cervical region are combined and classified using a support vector machine to detect endotracheal tube presence, then multiple thresholds determine the tube tip location.
25467807.headline_result: Az (AUC) 0.943+/-0.009 for tube detection; tip location error 1.89+/-2.01 mm

24282501.model_family: machine learning (unspecified classifier) on structural connectivity networks
24282501.clinical_problem: Predicting neurological outcome in neonates with neonatal encephalopathy using brain structural connectivity networks derived from diffusion tractography.
24282501.patient_population: Cohort of patients with neonatal encephalopathy
24282501.model_description: Diffusion tractography-derived structural brain networks are mapped to a high-dimensional feature space and standard machine learning algorithms predict neurological outcome, validated with nested cross-validation.

18850125.model_family: artificial neural network / support vector regression
18850125.clinical_problem: Semi-automated segmentation of fetal ultrasound images to improve estimated fetal weight via standard biometric measurements.
18850125.patient_population: 215 fetuses; 103 used for weight estimation within 3 days of delivery
18850125.model_description: A semi-automated segmentation system measures biparietal diameter, head circumference, abdominal circumference, and femur length from fetal ultrasound images, feeding these into regression, artificial neural network, and support vector regression models to estimate fetal weight.
18850125.headline_result: Mean absolute percentage error reduced from 6.71% (manual) to 4.66% (computerized)

40250104.clinical_problem: Integrating multimodal brain imaging (fMRI, DTI, sMRI) to predict cognitive function and characterize brain connectivity during youth development.
40250104.patient_population: Human Connectome Project Development (HCP-D) cohort of youth
40250104.model_description: A graph neural network integrates functional connectivity (fMRI), structural connectivity (DTI), and anatomical features (sMRI) parcellated with the Glasser atlas, using a masking strategy for interpretability, to predict cognitive function and analyze brain connectivity in youth.
40250104.study_design: retrospective cohort study using a public multimodal neuroimaging dataset

37774112.exclusion_reason: Clinical/biomarker prediction model for pre-eclampsia using maternal characteristics, serum biomarkers, and a Doppler pulsatility-index value; not an image-analysis AI model.

38461322.clinical_problem: Automated quality assessment and view/plane segmentation for fetal echocardiography to support the 18-22 week anomaly scan.
38461322.patient_population: 5,363 images from 2,551 pregnancies (training/validation); 100 patients prospective validation (192 images)
38461322.model_description: A deep learning model auto-captures and segments fetal echocardiography images, assigning a quality score that determines segmentation reliability, validated prospectively against clinician review.
38461322.dataset_size: 5,363 images from 2,551 pregnancies; prospective validation of 192 images from 100 patients
38461322.headline_result: Overall segmentation accuracy 0.91 (SD 0.09); 0.97 for above-average quality images
38461322.study_design: retrospective model development with prospective clinical validation

38701657.clinical_problem: Estimating white matter fiber orientation distribution in newborns and fetuses from limited diffusion MRI measurements, enabling microstructure assessment when only a few measurements are feasible.
38701657.patient_population: Newborn and fetal diffusion MRI datasets, external clinical validation datasets, and post-mortem histological validation
38701657.model_description: A deep learning model maps as few as six diffusion-weighted MRI measurements to fiber orientation distribution functions, trained against multi-shell high-angular-resolution ground truth, validated across scanners and against histology.
38701657.headline_result: Agreement rate 77.5%/22.2% for 1/2-fiber voxels (3%/5.4% higher than other DL methods); angular error 10/20 degrees (6/5 degrees lower)
38701657.study_design: retrospective methods development with external and histological validation

38758252.exclusion_reason: Study explicitly excludes pediatric radiographs from its cohort; adult chest radiograph population only.

38800118.clinical_problem: Reviewing how AI (machine learning, NLP, neural networks, computer vision) can be applied throughout pregnancy for early detection, monitoring and risk assessment of feto-maternal health.
38800118.model_description: Narrative review describing applications of AI subfields (machine learning, NLP, artificial neural networks, computer vision) across feto-maternal healthcare, including fetal ultrasound analysis for abnormality detection.

38824716.clinical_problem: Synthesizing anatomically accurate fetal head standard-plane ultrasound images to augment training data for automated fetal head standard-plane classification.
38824716.model_description: A conditional GAN uses class activation maps as priors during adversarial training to generate synthetic fetal head standard-plane ultrasound images, used to augment classifier training data.
38824716.headline_result: Frechet inception distance 88.52; classifier accuracy improved by 3.2% using synthetic images

38984984.clinical_problem: Predicting 2-year neurodevelopmental outcome (death or impairment) in neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy using multisequence brain MRI and basic clinical variables.
38984984.patient_population: 414 term neonates from the HEAL trial across 17 institutions
38984984.model_description: A deep learning classifier takes T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and diffusion tensor MRI plus sex and gestational age as input to predict death or neurodevelopmental impairment at 2 years.
38984984.study_design: retrospective secondary analysis of multicenter randomized trial data (HEAL trial), with in- and out-of-distribution testing

36752863.exclusion_reason: Radiomics feature reproducibility study (intraclass correlation of 2D vs 3D ROIs); no machine learning/AI predictive model applied.

36755050.clinical_problem: Automated classification and segmentation of the placenta on obstetric ultrasound to standardize detection of placenta previa.
36755050.patient_population: 7,500 training images; 100 second-trimester images from Barcelona (cross-validation cohort)
36755050.model_description: A deep learning model trained on manually annotated ultrasound images classifies and segments the placenta, compared against annotations from 25 clinicians of varying experience.
36755050.headline_result: Classification accuracy 81%; IoU 0.78 (model) vs 0.75 (best clinician); external cohort accuracy 76%, IoU 0.68

36794166.model_family: machine learning (KNN, random forest, SVM, LightGBM)
36794166.clinical_problem: Predicting extrathyroidal extension of papillary thyroid carcinoma in children and adolescents using ultrasound radiomics.
36794166.patient_population: 164 pediatric patients with papillary thyroid cancer
36794166.model_description: Radiomics features extracted from ultrasound images of thyroid tumors are used to train and compare KNN, random forest, SVM, and LightGBM models to predict extrathyroidal extension, with SHAP used for interpretability.
36794166.study_design: retrospective cohort study, randomized to training/validation cohorts

36980083.clinical_problem: Systematically reviewing diagnostic performance of AI-based computer-aided detection/diagnosis systems across pediatric radiology subspecialties.
36980083.model_description: Systematic review of 23 studies evaluating AI-based CAD applications across pediatric brain, respiratory, musculoskeletal, urologic and cardiac imaging, especially pneumonia detection.
36980083.headline_result: Most studies reported AUC>=0.83, sensitivity>=0.84, specificity>=0.80, accuracy>=0.87

37161503.clinical_problem: Real-time decision support during fetal ultrasound to narrow the differential diagnosis of rare genetic syndromes based on observed phenotypic features.
37161503.patient_population: 549 perinatal phenotypes from two referral centers (France, UK)
37161503.model_description: At each step of a fetal ultrasound exam, a decision-support system suggests the next phenotypic feature to assess and outputs a ranked differential diagnosis of rare genetic syndromes.
37161503.headline_result: Ascertained diagnosis within top-10 list in 93% (full-phenotype) / 83% (stepwise) of syndromic cases; specificity 94-96%, sensitivity 84-99%
37161503.study_design: retrospective validation study using clinical data from two referral centers

37161929.clinical_problem: Classifying normal versus abnormal fetal heart ultrasound images and identifying ventricular septal defects to assist prenatal diagnosis of congenital heart disease.
37161929.model_description: YOLOv5 object detection models are trained on fetal echocardiography standard views to classify normal vs abnormal hearts and detect ventricular septal defects.
37161929.headline_result: YOLOv5n 82.93% accuracy on CHD test set; YOLOv5l 92.79% accuracy on VSD test set
37161929.study_design: retrospective model development and testing study

37193656.clinical_problem: Diagnosing developmental dysplasia of the hip in infants from ultrasound images using deep learning, according to the Graf classification.
37193656.patient_population: 60 infants (64 hips) with DDH, 131 healthy infants (262 hips), up to 6 months old
37193656.model_description: Pre-trained CNN models (SqueezeNet, MobileNet_v2, EfficientNet) are fine-tuned via transfer learning on hip ultrasound images to classify DDH versus normal hips, with Grad-CAM used for interpretability.
37193656.headline_result: Accuracy, precision, recall, and F-measure all 1.0

37352995.clinical_problem: Discusses the need for a pediatric-specific AI curriculum and the challenges of AI education in pediatric radiology.
37352995.model_description: Discusses differences between pediatric and adult imaging relevant to AI model development (modality use, radiation dose, growth-related anatomic change, disease prevalence) and outlines needs for a dedicated pediatric radiology AI education curriculum.
37352995.study_design: commentary/perspective on AI education and curriculum development

37371851.clinical_problem: Screening for high-risk fetuses with common and rare genetic syndromes (Trisomy 21/18/13 and others) using facial and anatomical features on prenatal ultrasound.
37371851.model_description: A ResNet-based deep neural network (Pgds-ResNet) analyzes fetal ultrasound images to screen for genetic syndromes, generating heatmaps highlighting abnormal facial/anatomic features.
37371851.study_design: retrospective model development and comparative evaluation study

37509498.clinical_problem: Reviewing the role of AI/deep learning applied to DTI and fMRI for early autism spectrum disorder diagnosis.
37509498.model_description: Survey reviewing machine learning and deep learning techniques applied to diffusion tensor imaging and functional MRI for autism diagnosis and detection.

37606663.exclusion_reason: Scan inclusion criteria required age >=18 years; adult-only non-contrast brain CT population.

37683097.exclusion_reason: Conventional EEG microstate and fMRI temporal-variability statistical/mediation analysis in adolescents with depression; no AI/ML classification model described; EEG is non-radiologic imaging.

37945573.clinical_problem: Automated measurement of temporalis muscle thickness (a marker of lean muscle mass) on brain MRI to generate normal growth charts from childhood through adulthood.
37945573.patient_population: 23,876 brain MRIs of healthy subjects ages 4-35, plus validation in children with brain tumors
37945573.model_description: An automated deep learning pipeline measures temporalis muscle thickness (iTMT) on routine brain MRI, generating sex-specific normal growth charts with percentiles across ages 4-35.
37945573.study_design: retrospective cohort study with automated deep learning pipeline and multi-group validation

37999160.clinical_problem: Reviewing machine learning methods (classification, detection, segmentation) applied to fetal ultrasound images for anomaly detection.
37999160.model_description: Review of recent machine learning approaches for fetal ultrasound anomaly detection, covering classification, object recognition, and segmentation tasks.

38188914.clinical_problem: Detecting wrist fractures in children on radiographs using an optimized object detection algorithm.
38188914.model_description: A YOLOv7 object detection model, optimized through data preprocessing and configuration tuning, detects wrist fractures on pediatric radiographs; Grad-CAM used to visualize model attention.
38188914.headline_result: mAP@0.5 improved up to +25.51%, mAP@[0.5:0.95] improved up to +39.78% from preprocessing optimization
38188914.study_design: retrospective model development and optimization study using a public dataset

34191735.model_family: deep neural network + exclusivity regularized machine (meta-learning)
34191735.clinical_problem: Computer-aided diagnosis of developmental dysplasia of the hip in infants using B-mode ultrasound.
34191735.model_description: A two-stage meta-learning framework combining a deep neural network with an exclusivity regularized machine classifies infant hip ultrasound images for DDH diagnosis.

35063289.clinical_problem: Automated detection of low-lying placenta or placenta previa from 2D ultrasound in a resource-limited setting using low-cost equipment.
35063289.model_description: A U-Net deep learning model segments the placenta on 2D ultrasound images, and the segmentation is used to classify placental position as normal or low-lying/previa; deployed in real time on a smartphone with low-cost ultrasound.
35063289.dataset_size: 280 pregnant women, 6,574 training images; 148 holdout test cases
35063289.study_design: retrospective methods development and evaluation study in a resource-limited setting

35204353.clinical_problem: Predicting mitosis-karyorrhexis index (MKI) status of pediatric neuroblastoma non-invasively using PET/CT radiomics to guide further management.
35204353.model_description: Radiomics features extracted from 18F-FDG PET/CT images, selected via XGBoost, are combined with clinical characteristics into a radiomics nomogram predicting MKI status.

35246986.clinical_problem: Predicting neurodevelopmental disorders (ADHD, cognitive deficits in preterm infants) from brain connectome data derived from MRI.
35246986.patient_population: ADHD-200 dataset (adolescents) and Cincinnati Early Prediction Study (CINEPS) very preterm infant cohort
35246986.model_description: A deep convolutional neural network with multiple vector-shaped filters (ConCeptCNN) extracts topological features from brain connectome matrices to classify ADHD and predict cognitive deficits in very preterm infants.
35246986.headline_result: 78.7% accuracy for ADHD detection; 81.6% accuracy for cognitive deficit prediction in preterm infants
35246986.study_design: retrospective cohort study using public and institutional datasets

35281250.clinical_problem: Improving accuracy and consistency of bone age assessment among physicians of varying experience using AI-assisted reading of hand radiographs.
35281250.model_description: A deep learning convolutional neural network estimates bone age from hand radiographs, providing AI-assisted information to physicians to compare against unassisted assessments.
35281250.headline_result: MAE with AI 0.325/0.344/0.370 (senior/mid/junior) vs without AI 0.403/0.469/0.755, all p<0.001
35281250.study_design: retrospective reader study comparing physician performance with and without AI assistance

35281798.exclusion_reason: Uses large public chest radiograph collections without a stated pediatric-specific cohort; pediatric relevance for lateral CXR/TB detection is mentioned only as motivation, not as the study population.

35299255.exclusion_reason: Statistical reference-curve modeling (LMS growth-chart algorithm) of endocrine biomarkers; not an AI/ML imaging analysis. Ultrasound organ volume is only one of many biomarkers considered.

35361575.model_family: machine learning (6 candidate classifiers, sparse regression feature selection)
35361575.clinical_problem: Differentiating pediatric embryonal tumors, high-grade gliomas, and ependymomas using MRI radiomics to aid diagnosis, risk stratification, and treatment planning.
35361575.patient_population: 231 patients from 7 institutions (50 embryonal tumors, 127 high-grade gliomas, 54 ependymomas)
35361575.model_description: PyRadiomics features extracted from T2-weighted and gadolinium-enhanced T1-weighted MRI are reduced via sparse regression and used to train classifiers distinguishing pediatric supratentorial tumor types.
35361575.headline_result: AUC 0.98 (embryonal vs high-grade glioma), 0.82 (embryonal vs ependymoma), 0.96 (high-grade glioma vs ependymoma)

35460355.clinical_problem: Non-invasive prediction of MYCN gene amplification status in pediatric neuroblastoma using CT radiomics as a surrogate imaging biomarker.
35460355.model_description: Morphologic and radiomics texture features from contrast-enhanced CT are used to train an XGBoost model predicting MYCN amplification status, with accumulated local effects plots for interpretability.

35727944.clinical_problem: Characterizing white matter diffusion abnormalities in pediatric mild traumatic brain injury using multicompartmental diffusion models, and testing whether diffusion metrics improve diagnostic accuracy over clinical standards.
35727944.patient_population: 203 patients (8-18 years) and 170 matched healthy controls
35727944.model_description: Multicompartmental diffusion MRI models generate intracellular and free-water volume-fraction metrics; a random forest machine learning classifier uses these diffusion metrics alongside clinical standards to classify patients versus controls.
35727944.headline_result: Diffusion abnormalities increased overall diagnostic accuracy by ~10% over clinical gold standards

35731736.clinical_problem: Diagnosing cystic hygroma on first-trimester fetal ultrasound using deep learning.
35731736.patient_population: 289 sagittal fetal ultrasound images (129 cystic hygroma cases, 160 normal NT controls)
35731736.model_description: A DenseNet convolutional neural network classifies first-trimester fetal ultrasound images as cystic hygroma or normal, with Grad-CAM used to assess interpretability.
35731736.study_design: retrospective case-control study with internal validation

35809969.clinical_problem: Accurately estimating the diffusion tensor from few diffusion-weighted MRI measurements to enable shorter scans in non-cooperative patients such as neonates and infants.
35809969.model_description: Two sequential transformer networks estimate the diffusion tensor from as few as six diffusion-weighted measurements by learning relationships between diffusion signals and tensors in neighboring voxels.
35809969.headline_result: Estimations with 6 measurements comparable to standard methods using 30-88 measurements

35821715.exclusion_reason: COVID-19 vaccination epidemiology cohort study in school-aged children; no imaging or AI/ML component.

36093915.model_family: deep learning (unrolled neural network, DL-ESPIRiT variant)
36093915.clinical_problem: Accelerating 2D phase-contrast cardiac MRI flow measurements in children using deep learning reconstruction while maintaining accurate quantitative flow measurements.
36093915.patient_population: 155 fully sampled pediatric datasets (training); prospective cohort of 5 pediatric patients
36093915.model_description: A deep learning image-reconstruction framework (CD-DL) with Complex Difference estimation reconstructs highly undersampled 2D phase-contrast cardiac MRI, trained on pediatric datasets and validated retrospectively and prospectively against parallel imaging/compressed sensing methods.
36093915.headline_result: 9x acceleration within +/-5% accuracy/precision; peak velocity error 2.8% vs 3.9% (PICS)
36093915.study_design: retrospective and prospective model development/validation study

36260613.clinical_problem: Screening for biliary atresia in infants with jaundice using hepatobiliary ultrasound images and deep learning to assist non-specialist physicians.
36260613.patient_population: 180 patients (41 biliary atresia, 139 non-biliary atresia), 1,976 ultrasound images
36260613.model_description: Multiple deep learning CNN architectures (including ShuffleNet) classify hepatobiliary ultrasound images as biliary atresia or non-biliary atresia; a 'positive-dominance law' combines per-image predictions into a patient-level diagnosis.

36551961.exclusion_reason: Review of MRI radiogenomics in glioblastoma; adult brain tumor, not pediatric-specific.

36728734.exclusion_reason: General review of CT iterative reconstruction techniques; not specifically pediatric, with AI mentioned only briefly as a future perspective.

33647632.clinical_problem: Differentiating pediatric nonalcoholic fatty liver disease from healthy liver on ultrasound using texture-based machine learning classification.
33647632.patient_population: 93 normal subjects (484 ROIs), 39 NAFLD subjects (260 ROIs); external validation cohort of 42 children
33647632.model_description: Texture features extracted from regions of interest on hepatic ultrasound images are used to train an ensembled machine learning model (SVM, neural network, XGBoost) to classify liver images as NAFLD or normal.
33647632.dataset_size: 132 subjects total (93 normal, 39 NAFLD) plus a 42-child external validation cohort
33647632.headline_result: Ensembled ML model superior to intensity-based indices in external validation of 211 ROIs from 42 children
33647632.study_design: cross-sectional study with external validation cohort

33711613.exclusion_reason: Markerless video-based motion capture/pose estimation for gait analysis; uses RGB video, not a radiologic imaging modality (X-ray/CT/MRI/US).

33734521.exclusion_reason: Conventional resting-state fMRI functional connectivity analysis of subconcussive head impacts in youth football; no AI/ML model described.

33891778.clinical_problem: Automatically assessing image quality of reconstructed 3D fetal brain MRI to reduce the need for time-consuming manual visual inspection.
33891778.patient_population: 271 MR exams from 211 fetuses (mean gestational age 30.9+/-5.5 weeks)
33891778.model_description: Three multi-instance deep learning models (count-based, vote-based, feature-embedding) classify 3D fetal brain MRI reconstructions as high or low quality, optionally using gestational age as an input.
33891778.headline_result: Best model (MI-CB-DLM with gestational age): accuracy 0.86, AUC 0.93
33891778.study_design: retrospective methods development and validation study

34071202.clinical_problem: Reviewing deep learning techniques applied to pediatric brain tumor imaging (diagnosis, classification, segmentation) and associated challenges.
34071202.model_description: Narrative review summarizing deep learning research on pediatric brain tumor MRI/CT imaging, including diagnostic clues (age, location, incidence) and technical/medical limitations.

34096674.exclusion_reason: Automated signal-processing algorithm (myocardial velocity trace integration) for measuring cardiac excursion; no explicit AI/ML method described.

34240783.clinical_problem: Estimating brain-predicted age difference (BrainPAD) from multimodal MRI (morphometry and connectomes) as an indicator of psychiatric and cognitive functioning in youth.
34240783.patient_population: 489 participants from the Healthy Brain Network (training/test split)
34240783.model_description: A stacked ensemble AutoML approach combines multiple machine learning algorithms applied to brain morphometry and white matter connectome features from MRI to estimate brain-predicted age difference (BrainPAD), a marker linked to psychiatric symptoms.
34240783.headline_result: MAE 1.18 years (combined model); MAE 0.26 years after ComBat harmonization
34240783.study_design: retrospective cohort study using a public dataset

34357510.model_family: CNN (transfer learning: Inception ResNet v2, MobileNetV2)
34357510.clinical_problem: Automatically measuring hip migration percentage on pelvis radiographs to assess hip displacement in children with cerebral palsy.
34357510.model_description: Two fine-tuned CNNs (Inception ResNet v2, then MobileNetV2) detect landmark locations on pelvis radiographs to automatically calculate hip migration percentage.
34357510.headline_result: Mean absolute difference 4.5+/-4.3%, ICC 0.91; sensitivity/specificity 87.8%/93.4% (30% MP threshold)
34357510.study_design: retrospective methods development and validation study

34368247.clinical_problem: Identifying risk factors, including pre-operative echocardiographic right ventricular function, for post-operative complications after Tetralogy of Fallot repair in children.
34368247.patient_population: 162 children <2 years with Tetralogy of Fallot undergoing surgical repair
34368247.model_description: Gradient-boosted machine learning models use patient, operative, and echocardiographic variables (including pre-operative RV strain and fractional area change) to identify predictors of post-operative cardiac complications.
34368247.headline_result: 26.5% had at least one post-operative complication; cardiopulmonary bypass duration was the highest-ranked predictor

34392363.model_family: sequential machine learning classifier (logistic regression, neural network)
34392363.clinical_problem: Distinguishing pediatric posterior fossa tumor types (pilocytic astrocytoma, medulloblastoma, ependymoma) on MRI to aid diagnosis and surgical planning.
34392363.model_description: A 2-step sequential machine-learning classifier first distinguishes pilocytic astrocytoma from other tumors using T2/T1 radiomics features (logistic regression), then distinguishes medulloblastoma from ependymoma (neural network) using MRI Image Biomarker Standardization Initiative features.
34392363.dataset_size: 527 patients (274 medulloblastoma, 156 pilocytic astrocytoma, 97 ependymoma), multinational
34392363.headline_result: F1 scores: 0.8809 (PA vs non-PA), 0.9189 (MB vs EP), 0.9179 combined

34428783.exclusion_reason: Standard fMRI activation comparison study of visuospatial working memory and arithmetic; no AI/ML model.

34476196.clinical_problem: Reducing contrast medium and radiation dose in pediatric coronary CT angiography using deep learning image reconstruction while maintaining image quality.
34476196.patient_population: 27 pediatric arrhythmic patients (study group), 27 matched controls
34476196.model_description: A deep learning image-reconstruction algorithm processes low-dose, low-contrast coronary CT angiography scans acquired at 70 kVp with a shortened contrast-injection protocol, compared to standard-dose scans reconstructed with iterative reconstruction.
34476196.headline_result: Contrast dose reduced 53% to 15.07+/-3.68 mL; radiation dose reduced 36% to 0.57+/-0.31 mSv; similar image quality scores

34518201.exclusion_reason: Newborn gestational-age estimation using anthropometric and physical-exam features (birth weight, head/chest circumference, foot length, etc.); no imaging component.

34610500.clinical_problem: Automated segmentation of all four fetal cardiac chambers on echocardiography to assist diagnosis of fetal heart disease.
34610500.model_description: A Category Attention Instance Segmentation Network with category, mask, and category-attention branches segments all four fetal cardiac chambers simultaneously from echocardiography images.
34610500.headline_result: Dice coefficients 0.7956/0.7619/0.8199/0.7470 for the four chambers; average precision 45.64%

34870211.clinical_problem: Enabling reduced-dose FDG PET/MRI in children and young adults with lymphoma using deep learning image augmentation while preserving accurate treatment response assessment.

34173089.headline_result: average precision 0.977 (NGT), 0.989 (ETT), 0.979 (UAC), 0.937 (UVC) on the test set
34173089.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and internal validation study

34752491.model_family: machine learning and deep learning (planned; 3D U-Net for lung segmentation)
34752491.clinical_problem: predicting postnatal pulmonary hypertension and related outcomes in congenital diaphragmatic hernia from prenatal clinical and imaging data

34752491.model_description: Study protocol for machine-learning and deep-learning forecasting models that take integrated clinical and fetal MRI data as input and will output prediction of postnatal pulmonary hypertension and related outcomes, plus a planned 3D U-Net-based automatic fetal lung segmentation tool for MRI.
34752491.study_design: retrospective study protocol for machine-learning/deep-learning outcome-prediction models, registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04609163)

34814276.clinical_problem: automated measurement of fetal femur length on ultrasound
34814276.model_description: Takes a fetal femur ultrasound image as input and outputs an automatic measurement of femur length, comparing a random forest regression model that detects femur endpoints against a SegNet-based deep learning segmentation approach.

34814276.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and comparative evaluation study

32025833.exclusion_reason: quantitative texture-analysis study of infant brain MRI using conventional statistics (regression, ROC); no AI/ML model built

32190035.model_family: U-Net segmentation with deep active learning, CNN feature extraction (transfer learning), and ensemble regression
32190035.clinical_problem: automated bone age assessment for skeletal maturity in children

32190035.headline_result: mean discrepancy between predicted and actual bone age of 6.96 months (male) and 7.35 months (female); segmentation Dice score 0.95
32190035.study_design: retrospective algorithm development on a public dataset

32619065.exclusion_reason: magnetoencephalography connectomic analysis using partial least squares; MEG is not a standard radiologic imaging modality and the method is a conventional multivariate statistical technique, not an AI/ML model

32969025.model_family: U-Net+ResNet deep learning segmentation with fuzzy c-means clustering
32969025.clinical_problem: automated segmentation and longitudinal follow-up of optic pathway gliomas in children
32969025.patient_population: 29 pediatric patients with chiasmatic optic pathway glioma, 202 MRI scans, scanned longitudinally
32969025.model_description: Takes T2 and post-contrast T1-weighted brain MRI as input and outputs automatic segmentation of the optic pathway glioma tumor volume plus voxel-based classification into enhanced, non-enhanced, and cystic tumor components, using a U-Net+ResNet deep learning model and fuzzy c-means clustering.
32969025.headline_result: test-set Dice score 0.761±0.011, precision 0.794±0.028, recall 0.742±0.012; tumor-component classification accuracy 0.94
32969025.study_design: retrospective algorithm development with fivefold cross-validation

33123034.exclusion_reason: fMRI pilot study of face-processing hemispheric lateralization in children versus adults; conventional statistical comparison, no AI/ML component

31227881.clinical_problem: estimating fetal (conceptus) radiation dose during maternal CT imaging via automated patient-specific organ segmentation
31227881.model_description: Takes an abdominal CT scan of a pregnant patient as input and outputs automated segmentation of six anatomical structures (including the uterus), used to build a patient-specific computational phantom for Monte Carlo estimation of fetal (conceptus) radiation dose.
31227881.dataset_size: 32 CT exams augmented to 128 datasets (80%/20% train/test)
31227881.headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 0.92-0.98 for internal organs versus manual segmentation; mean uterus absorbed dose 2.9 mGy, organ dose differences -1.55% to 0.28%
31227881.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and internal validation study

31767194.exclusion_reason: narrative review/commentary on AI, big data, and automation in surgical practice generally; not focused on pediatric radiology imaging AI

31890287.exclusion_reason: review of wide-field retinal imaging for sickle cell retinopathy; retinal imaging is non-radiologic and out of scope

31992944.model_family: convolutional neural network (visual saliency prediction / gaze-point regression, transfer learning)
31992944.clinical_problem: improving automated detection of standard imaging planes in fetal anomaly screening ultrasound
31992944.patient_population: fetal anomaly screening ultrasound examinations, using a sonographer gaze-tracking dataset
31992944.model_description: Takes ultrasound video frames from fetal anomaly screening as input and outputs learned image representations by modeling sonographer visual attention (gaze), which are then fine-tuned for ultrasound standard-plane detection.
31992944.headline_result: fine-tuning the saliency-based representation improved standard-plane detection F1-score by 9.6% overall (15.3% for cardiac planes) over random initialization
31992944.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and evaluation study

32090205.clinical_problem: improving image quality of low-dose pediatric abdominal CT reconstructed with filtered back projection
32090205.patient_population: 11 pediatric abdominal CT exams for training; 20 low-dose pediatric CT datasets for evaluation
32090205.model_description: Takes a filtered-back-projection-reconstructed low-dose pediatric abdominal CT image as input and outputs a denoised image simulating iterative-reconstruction quality, using a residual CNN trained to predict the difference between FBP and iterative reconstruction, evaluated by two pediatric radiologists.
32090205.dataset_size: 11 CT exams for training; 20 low-dose datasets for evaluation
32090205.headline_result: image noise reduced by 31% with CNN (P<.001); CNN preferred over FBP for overall image quality by both readers
32090205.study_design: retrospective algorithm development with two-reader image quality evaluation

29844507.model_family: joint generalized additive model and machine-learning classifier
29844507.clinical_problem: identifying brain structural patterns associated with adolescent alcohol misuse while controlling for confounding factors
29844507.patient_population: 705 adolescents from the NCANDA baseline cohort
29844507.model_description: Takes macrostructural MRI and microstructural diffusion tensor imaging metrics as input and outputs a classification of high- versus low-drinking adolescents, using a joint machine-learning model that simultaneously removes confounding factors and identifies cohort-specific neuromorphometric patterns.
29844507.headline_result: an eight-brain-region pattern classified high-drinking adolescents more accurately than regions identified by alternative approaches
29844507.study_design: retrospective cross-sectional cohort study with machine-learning classification

28008075.exclusion_reason: fMRI developmental study of social-interaction perception via human motion; conventional group-level activation analysis, no AI/ML component

27737853.clinical_problem: relating brain network architecture from resting-state fMRI to intelligence in children with focal epilepsy
27737853.patient_population: 30 children (4-18 years) with focal epilepsy undergoing 3T brain MRI with resting-state fMRI
27737853.model_description: Takes resting-state fMRI-derived graph-theoretical network metrics (clustering coefficient, transitivity, modularity, path length, global efficiency) as input and outputs a machine-learning-based estimate of each metric's independent contribution to full-scale intelligence quotient.
27737853.headline_result: clustering coefficient and path length independently associated with full-scale IQ after adjusting for age and sex; longer epilepsy history associated with shorter path length (P=.008)
